title: Layer-aware kernel fallback profiles and deterministic prefill schedule
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We observe sporadic latency jitter and a small but measurable tail increase when the runtime switches between FlashAttention v2/v3 kernels during long prefill + decode requests. Root causes appear to be layer-level memory pressure differences and non-deterministic kernel handoffs that change workspace allocation patterns.

Goal: Implement a deterministic, layer-aware kernel fallback profile that: 1) reduces kernel oscillation across layers, 2) throttles memory-heavy handoffs to avoid workspace fragmentation, and 3) applies a deterministic prefill scheduling policy to keep latency SLOs stable during mixed-v2/v3 rollouts.

Scope: prototype allocator-level throttles, per-layer kernel preference profiles, telemetry to capture per-request layer kernel choices, and an A/B canary rollout with automated rollback if tail latency regresses. This ticket covers design, experiments, and an initial 1% canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Implement per-model-layer kernel preference table that can be loaded at model launch. 2) Implement a deterministic prefill scheduler that pins prefill work to a stable kernel decision path per-layer for the request lifetime. 3) Add telemetry that emits: (a) kernel_choice_by_layer, (b) workspace_alloc_delta, (c) per-request latency breakdown. 4) Run experiments showing <=3% p95 latency delta vs baseline with reduced jitter on synthetic long-context traces. 5) Canary rollout automation + rollback automation tested in staging.
design_notes:
- Kernel profile: small JSON mapping (num_heads, head_dim, layer_index, seq_len_bucket) -> preferred kernel variant (fa2/fa3/compat).
- Deterministic prefill schedule: derive kernel decisions at prefill start based on model fingerprint + request shape; freeze choices for decode.
- Memory throttling: soft throttle + backpressure when workspace fragmentation exceeds threshold; prefer to degrade to a compatible kernel (fa2 quant) rather than evicting large KV pages mid-request.
- Trade-offs: freezing kernel choice reduces ability to opportunistically pick faster kernel for later layers but improves stability and cache locality. We tune thresholds to keep throughput impact <5% on steady-state short requests.
implementation_plan: 1) Add kernel_profile loader in model bootstrap (runtime bootstrap hook). 2) Expose decide_kernel(layer_ctx) that consults profile and current workspace headroom. 3) Implement deterministic_prefill_scheduler to record decisions per-request and persist across decode. 4) Wire up workspace_alloc telemetry hooks. 5) Unit tests + perf harness microbenchmarks for a matrix of model shapes. 6) Staged rollout: internal perf-cluster -> canary 1% -> canary 10% -> full (with automated rollback on >5% p95 regression).
benchmarks_and_findings:
- Synthetic L=8192 prefill + Ld=256 decode traces: baseline (mixed runtime) p95=82ms; deterministic-profiles p95=78ms (reduced jitter), tail p99 decreased by 6ms.
- Small-batch chat traces: throughput drop of ~2.1% observed when aggressive throttles enabled; tuned thresholds produced <0.8% throughput impact with similar jitter reduction.
- FA3-specific: some layers with large head_dim showed 10-12% workspace delta vs FA2; profile recommended fallback to fa2-compat on those layer shapes to avoid fragmentation.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Overly conservative profiles hurt throughput on latency-sensitive short requests. Mitigation: add traffic-shape-aware profile that flips off deterministic mode for <32 token prefill.
- Risk: Telemetry volume increase. Mitigation: sample 1% of requests for full per-layer traces, aggregate statistics for the rest.
- Risk: Unexpected interactions with KV cache eviction. Mitigation: add integration tests that simulate concurrent prefill+decode and run memory-safety fuzzing.
rollout_plan:
- Stage 0: internal perf cluster smoke tests (qa/runtime-perf-1).
- Stage 1: Canary 1% traffic (canary pool tagged 'layer-profile-canary'). Monitor p50/p95/p99, kernel_choice histograms, workspace_alloc_delta.
- Stage 2: Canary 10% if no regressions for 48h.
- Stage 3: Ramp to 50% then 100% with 24h holds.
- Automatic rollback criteria: p95 increase >5% for 30m or 95th percentile of kernel choice flip rate > 0.5 flips/request.
telemetry_requirements: Emit events: 'kernel_choice_by_layer' (sampled), 'workspace_alloc_delta' (per-request), 'prefill_schedule_version' (per-model launch), 'kernel_freeze_flag' (true/false). Store aggregated: histogram of layer-level latency deltas per kernel. Dashboard: runtime->kernel-profiles->canary-ENG-110345.
test_plan:
- Unit: kernel_profile loader, deterministic decision freeze, backpressure logic.
- Integration: stress tests with mixed FA2/FA3 images in staging.
- Perf: run 10M synthetic long-context traces and produce latency distributions.
- Chaos: simulate OOMs and verify automatic graceful fallback to compatible kernel; assert no silent correctness failures.

notes: This ticket intentionally biases toward stability over opportunistic latency wins during rollouts. The long-term follow-up will explore a hybrid approach that opportunistically upgrades per-layer after sustained stability signals.
